pattern.notes: City Market is a public setting only; fictional stalls and traders.

ob.text: Customer Grace Adhiambo reports that florist Beatrice Kerubo (39), stall 39, City Market, was found behind the curtain of her stall's cold room at 12:10. Pronounced dead at the scene.

people.name: Beatrice Kerubo
people.bio: Started undercutting the market with cheap imported lilies this month. Her first box arrived yesterday.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, late 30s, white blouse, a measuring tape around her neck, a red rose behind one ear, confident grin, ID-photo framing

people.name: Lucy Kagendo
people.bio: Has sold lilies at City Market for ten years. The only lily seller in the aisle until this month.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, early 30s, hair wrapped in a bright kanga, canvas apron with orange pollen stains, armful of white lilies, tight polite smile, ID-photo framing

people.name: Josphat Kimani
people.bio: Sells roses two stalls the other side. His hands are covered in fresh scratches today.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 40s, green apron, both hands and forearms covered in fresh thorn scratches, holding a bundle of red roses, uneasy, ID-photo framing

people.name: Naliaka Simiyu
people.bio: Had a loud argument with Beatrice this morning about flower buckets blocking the aisle.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, around 50, beaded necklaces for sale draped over her arm, kitenge dress, indignant expression, ID-photo framing

people.name: Ahmed Yusuf
people.bio: His counter faces the flower aisle.

people.name: Grace Adhiambo
people.bio: Bought roses at 11:45 and came back at 12:10 for carnations.

people.name: Verger, All Saints Cathedral
people.bio: Received the wedding flowers. Statement by phone.

places.name: Grace's route between the market and her office

locations.name: City Market flower aisle
locations.description: Late morning under the high roof of City Market off Muindi Mbingu Street. Buckets of roses, carnations, lilies and gerberas line one aisle; curio sellers fill the next; butchers work at the far end. Each stall has its licence number on a painted board.

hotspots.label: Behind stall 39's cold-room curtain
hotspots.text: Beatrice lies behind the plastic curtain of her cold room. A flower-bucket stand is on its side. The report says one blow.

hotspots.label: Her blouse
hotspots.text: On the shoulder of her white blouse: bright orange stains in the shape of fingers.

hotspots.label: Stall 39's cold room
hotspots.text: Buckets of roses and carnations. In the corner, a cardboard box marked LILIES — IMPORT.

hotspots.label: Market master's licence board
hotspots.text: A painted board by the aisle entrance lists every stall by number, holder and product.

hotspots.label: Stall 37 (roses)
hotspots.text: The rose stall. A young apprentice is de-thorning stems with a knife; his hands are scratched too.

hotspots.label: Ahmed's butchery counter
hotspots.text: Ahmed Yusuf's counter faces the flower aisle directly.

image.brief: the flower aisle of Nairobi City Market under a high iron roof, buckets of red roses, white lilies and orange gerberas, painted stall number boards, a plastic strip curtain over a cold room, no people

body.label: Orange pollen, finger-shaped, on the left shoulder. Lily pollen stains everything and won't wash out (florists' saying).

image.brief: close-up of the shoulder of a white cotton blouse with bright orange lily-pollen stains in the shape of four fingers, no person visible

body.label: Box: LILIES — IMPORT. Tape still sealed. Inside: closed buds, no open flowers, no pollen.
Fresh scratches on both hands and forearms.
Canvas apron, fresh orange smears down the front, still damp from being rubbed.

facts.text: Beatrice Kerubo was found behind the cold-room curtain of stall 39 at 12:10.
Beatrice was struck once with her own flower-bucket stand.
Orange pollen in the shape of fingers stains the shoulder of her blouse, as if someone grabbed her.
Bright orange pollen like that comes from lilies.
Beatrice's own lily box is still sealed: closed buds, no pollen.
Licence board: the only stall selling lilies is stall 41, L. Kagendo.
Ahmed saw Lucy walk back from stall 39 to stall 41 at about 11:55, wiping her hands hard on her apron.
Ahmed: the curio seller Naliaka Simiyu shouted at Beatrice about buckets in the aisle this morning.
Ahmed served two customers at his counter between 11:40 and 12:10; both remember him.
Lucy's apron is freshly smeared with orange pollen down the front.
Grace bought roses from Beatrice at 11:45. She was fine.
Grace's matatu receipts: to her office at 11:48 and back at 12:06.
Josphat Kimani's hands are covered in fresh scratches.
Apprentice: they de-thorned forty dozen roses this morning for a wedding. Everyone on the rose stall is scratched.
Verger: Josphat delivered and arranged the wedding flowers at All Saints Cathedral from 11:30 to 12:15.
Naliaka's City Hall slip: queued from 11:20, paid at 12:02, signed out at the gate at 12:12.
Lucy: "I've been at my stall all morning. Ask anyone."
Lucy: "Beatrice and I compete. That's the market. I didn't touch her."
Lucy says Beatrice was selling imported lilies at half her price.
Josphat: "I was at the cathedral with the wedding flowers."
Naliaka: "Yes, I shouted at her. Then I went to City Hall to pay my fees."

interrogations.intro: Grace still holds the roses she bought. "I only came back for carnations."

topics.reply: She gave me an extra rose for free and said, 'Next week, lilies, half price, tell your friends.'

interrogations.intro: Ahmed wipes his cleaver and sets it down carefully, away from Amani. "Ask me. I see the whole aisle from here."

topics.reply: The lily lady? About five to twelve she walked back from Beatrice's side to her own stall, rubbing her hands on her apron like they were dirty.
The curio mama shouted at Beatrice this morning about buckets in the aisle. Then she went off with her fee book.
Kimani left early with his wedding flowers in a pickup. Half eleven, maybe.

interrogations.intro: Lucy keeps arranging lilies while she talks. Her apron is orange down the front.

topics.reply: She brought in imported lilies at half my price. Half! Ten years I've sold lilies in this market.
Everyone in this aisle has pollen on them. It's a flower market.

interrogations.intro: Josphat comes back from the cathedral and stops when he sees the tape. He hides his hands behind his back without meaning to.

topics.reply: Forty dozen roses de-thorned since six this morning! Look at the boy's hands, look at mine. Call the cathedral.

interrogations.intro: Naliaka arrives back with her receipt held up like a flag. "I know what Ahmed told you. Here."

topics.reply: We shouted about buckets. Every week we shout about buckets. It's the soko.

prosecutor.pass: Lily pollen on her shoulder, and one lily seller in the market, seen wiping her hands. That will hold.
fail: This doesn't hold up. Scratched hands are not a confession. What did the killer leave on her?
No. Where did that pollen come from? Not from her own box.

proof.concludes: The lily pollen on her shoulder didn't come from her own stock, which was still sealed. The attacker had lily pollen on their hands.
Only Lucy Kagendo handles lilies in the market, and she was seen walking back from stall 39 at 11:55 wiping orange hands on her apron.

eliminations.why: Josphat was at All Saints Cathedral from 11:30 to 12:15; his scratches come from de-thorning forty dozen roses.
Naliaka was in the City Hall fee queue from 11:20 and signed out of its gate at 12:12.
Ahmed was serving two customers at his own counter the whole time.
Grace left after buying roses at 11:45 and her matatu receipts cover the time until she came back at 12:10.

reconstruction.text: This month Beatrice starts selling imported lilies at half Lucy's price. Ten years of Lucy's trade, undercut in a week.
About 11:50. Lucy walks over to stall 39 with lily pollen still on her hands from her own buckets, to 'talk'.
Beatrice laughs at her. Lucy grabs her by the shoulder and hits her with the bucket stand.
11:55. Lucy walks back to stall 41 rubbing her hands on her apron, and goes on selling lilies.
Across the market, Josphat Kimani stands in All Saints Cathedral arranging forty dozen roses, his hands scratched raw by the thorns. Suspicion isn't evidence.

tier1.line: The killer left something on her. Florists will tell you: that colour doesn't come from roses.

tier2.line: Her own lilies were still sealed. Read the licence board: who else sells them?

glossary.def: Respectful way to address or refer to an older woman.
Printed cotton cloth worn as a wrap or headscarf.
Brightly printed cotton cloth and the clothes made from it.

ui.beatNotes: First red herring: the scratched hands, explained in the evidence and in the reconstruction. First hint offer: after one wrong submission, Mwalimu's number lights up on the desk phone and she explains the three hint tiers in one sentence each.
hintOfferLines: First call, Detective, and it's free in every way but stars. I'll tell you where to look.
Second call: I'll show you two facts that belong together.
Third call: I'll fill a blank for you. Then it's only one star, and you'll know why.
